question: What is the primary purpose of evaluation techniques in nursing education?

options.A: To punish students who fail examinations
options.B: To gather data on learning and ensure safe clinical competence
options.D: To increase the workload of nursing educators

explanation: Evaluation techniques systematically gather data regarding student learning and clinical competence to ensure they meet professional standards and protect public safety. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h1)

question: Which regulatory body sets standards that Nigerian nursing students must meet through proper educational evaluation?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN)
options.C: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN) establishes the standards of practice and competence that nursing students must achieve and demonstrate. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following best describes formative evaluation?

options.A: A final exam given at the end of the nursing program
options.B: Continuous feedback provided during the learning process to identify gaps
options.C: A graded licensure examination by the NMCN
options.D: A test that determines graduation eligibility exclusively

explanation: Formative evaluation happens during the learning process, offering continuous feedback to help students correct errors and improve before final tests. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h2)

question: When is a summative evaluation typically conducted?

options.A: At the end of an instructional unit or program to measure final achievement
options.B: Before any teaching or clinical posting begins
options.C: During daily bedside handovers as casual conversation
options.D: Only when a student requests remediation

explanation: Summative evaluations take place at the conclusion of a course or program to measure final achievement and decide progression. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h2)

question: What does the assessment of the cognitive domain primarily focus on?

options.B: Acquisition of knowledge, critical thinking, and theory

explanation: The cognitive domain involves mental skills, knowledge acquisition, and critical thinking regarding nursing theory and clinical judgment. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h3)

question: Which tool is commonly used to assess higher-level cognitive skills in nursing students?

options.A: Case study analyses and problem-solving questions

explanation: Case study analyses challenge students to apply theory, prioritize care, and solve complex clinical problems, reflecting higher-level cognition. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h3)

question: Which of the following is a primary focus when assessing the psychomotor domain?

options.B: Physical coordination and execution of hands-on nursing procedures

explanation: The psychomotor domain centers on physical movement, motor skills, and the manual execution of clinical procedures like wound care. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h4)

question: What is a major benefit of using simulation for psychomotor evaluation?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any written exams
options.B: It allows students to practice and be evaluated on procedures safely without risking patient harm
options.C: It removes the need for clinical instructors
options.D: It guarantees 100% distinction grades for every student

explanation: Simulation provides a controlled environment where students can master psychomotor skills on mannequins without risking actual patient safety. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h4)

question: What does the affective domain in nursing education primarily evaluate?

options.B: Attitudes, values, ethics, and professional demeanor

explanation: The affective domain addresses attitudes, values, ethics, empathy, and professional behaviors expected of a professional nurse. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h5)

question: Which method is commonly used by nursing educators to assess affective development?

options.A: Reflective journals and clinical observation of professional interactions

explanation: Reflective journals and direct observation of student-patient interactions help educators evaluate ethical reasoning and professional values. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h5)

question: How does a clinical checklist differ primarily from a rating scale?

options.A: Checklists only measure theory, while rating scales measure practice
options.B: Checklists indicate the presence or absence of specific steps, whereas rating scales measure the quality of performance
options.C: Checklists are completed by patients, while rating scales are completed by doctors
options.D: Checklists are illegal in Nigerian nursing schools

explanation: Checklists record whether specific steps were done or not done, while rating scales evaluate the degree or quality of how well those actions were performed. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h6)

question: When is a rating scale most appropriately used in clinical nursing evaluations?

options.A: When evaluating the quality of complex behaviors like communication and organization
options.B: When simply counting the number of bandages in a tray
options.C: When grading a multiple-choice midterm exam

explanation: Rating scales evaluate the quality or proficiency of complex, flowing clinical tasks such as patient communication and bedside organization. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary benefit of encouraging student self-assessment?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for clinical instructors
options.B: It encourages students to reflect on their performance and take ownership of their learning
options.C: It guarantees that every student receives a top grade
options.D: It eliminates all forms of written examinations

explanation: Self-assessment promotes critical self-reflection, helping students identify their own strengths and weaknesses to become self-directed learners. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h7)

question: What is essential for peer evaluation to be successful in a nursing class?

options.A: Allowing students to grade each other based entirely on personal friendships
options.B: Providing clear evaluation criteria and training on how to give objective feedback
options.C: Keeping the feedback hidden from the instructor and the student being reviewed
options.D: Using it only for high-stakes final grading without rubrics

explanation: Clear rubrics and training on objective feedback are vital to prevent bias and ensure constructive, professional peer evaluations. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h7)

question: What does validity mean in the context of nursing assessments?

options.A: The assessment tool measures what it is intended to measure
options.B: The exam is printed on high-quality paper
options.C: Every student passes the test on the first attempt
options.D: The test takes less than thirty minutes to complete

explanation: Validity ensures that an assessment accurately measures the specific knowledge, skill, or attitude it claims to evaluate. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h8)

question: Why is reliability important for clinical evaluation tools?

options.A: It ensures that different instructors will yield consistent and dependable scores for the same performance
options.B: It allows students to grade their own papers without faculty input
options.C: It guarantees that exams are conducted only online
options.D: It reduces the total number of clinical hours required by the NMCN

explanation: Reliability guarantees consistency, meaning different evaluators using the same tool will give similar, dependable scores for equivalent student performance. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h8)
